lines.text: Every evening at 6:05, this woman runs downstairs into the corner diner and asks for one thing: a glass of water.
Before the cook can pour it, he grabs two pans and slams them together right behind her.
She jumps, she smiles, she says thank you, and she walks out without drinking a drop.
Theo, the night cashier, watches it happen every single evening, and it's driving him crazy.
Then one evening, Marco the cook is off sick, and something strange happens.
The new cook just hands her the water, and she drinks the whole glass.
But this time, no smile. No thank you. She leaves looking worse.
Theo checks the water. It's fine, and no other customer does this.
So why does she thank the man who scares her, and not the one who gives her water?
You have ten seconds. Comment your answer now.
Time's up.
The next evening, Theo replays the diner camera in slow motion, and there it is.
Every few seconds, her shoulders jump.
Hic. Hic. Hic. She has the hiccups.
She never wanted the water. She wanted a fright.
The pans go bang, she jumps, and the hiccups stop.
The water didn't work, so she left still hiccuping.
Theo laughs so hard he knocks over the straws.
The next morning, he hangs two spare pans by the register, just in case.
So, did you get it right? Follow for more.
